% Locally authored, not taken from the desktop examples.
%
% Every other corpus project loads fontenc, which routes XeTeX through TFM
% metrics and Type 1 fonts. This one deliberately does not, so XeTeX takes its
% default Unicode path and resolves Latin Modern as an actual OpenType file.
% That path had never been executed by any corpus run, and the first document
% typed into the product found it: the font resolved remotely, was saved under
% a name carrying no extension, and xdvipdfmx could not identify it.
%
% There is no reference PDF: those come from desktop Tectonic and cannot be
% produced here. This entry answers "does it compile and render", not "does it
% match desktop".
\documentclass{article}

\title{Default font path}
\author{Opal Web}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section{Text}

Ordinary text, \emph{emphasised text}, and \textbf{bold text}, so the roman,
italic and bold faces are all resolved rather than only the first.

\section{Mathematics}

Inline $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$ and displayed:
\[
  \int_0^1 x^2 \, \mathrm{d}x = \frac{1}{3}
\]

\section{A list}

\begin{itemize}
  \item A first item.
  \item A second item, with a \texttt{monospaced} word in it.
\end{itemize}

\end{document}
